name: float-field
title: Float Field
description: A text field whose label rises to the top edge on focus, with a ring that fades in and a shake for errors.

perf.budget: A native text input with three shared values: label, ring and shake. Nothing runs at rest.

measurements.notes: The run types into both fields; the janky frames are the keyboard opening and closing, not the field.

a11y.reducedMotion: The label moves without a spring and the field does not shake.
a11y.screenReader: A text field named by its label, with the hint or error as its hint; a new error is announced.
a11y.touchTarget: The whole field is the target, 56 pt tall.

meta.guide:
## Usage

```tsx
import { FloatField } from '@/components/kinetik/float-field';

<FloatField
  label="Email"
  hint="We only use it for receipts."
  error={invalid ? 'That does not look like an email address.' : undefined}
  value={email}
  onChangeText={setEmail}
  keyboardType="email-address"
  autoCapitalize="none"
/>;
```

## When to use

- Forms where space is tight and every field needs a visible name: sign up, checkout, profile.
- Fields that validate on blur and need to say what is wrong right under the input.

## When not to use

- Long text. Use Grow Area, which grows with what is typed.
- Search. A search field reads better with an icon and no floating label.

## Notes

- Every other `TextInput` prop (keyboard type, auto-complete, secure entry, return key) is passed through.
- The label is the field's accessible name and the hint or error is its hint; a new error is also announced.
- With reduced motion the label still moves, without a spring, and the field does not shake.

docs: Prefer `npx kinetik-ui add float-field`: it installs dependencies with expo install, so versions match your Expo SDK.
